key_insight: A two-stage LLM pipeline can surface many internal inconsistencies in discharge summaries, but reliable use depends on strong context-aware verification.
clinical_relevance: Automatically flagging contradictory or ambiguous documentation in EHR notes could support chart review, reduce reasoning errors, and improve patient safety.
method: Screened 3,000 randomly sampled MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries
Used Gemini 2.5 Pro for open-ended candidate inconsistency detection
Used Gemini 2.5 Flash for context-grounded verification, then had clinicians review a subset
evidence_signal: The pipeline generated 3,460 candidate inconsistencies across 69.7% of admissions, with expert review highlighting common failure modes tied to temporal reasoning and missing clinical context.
watch_item: Many flags are not true contradictions unless each statement is anchored to its section, timeline, and clinical domain, so deployment needs careful validation and human oversight.
paper_title: Toward Automated Detection of Documentation Inconsistencies in Electronic Health Records
